newsitem.title: UK: New Co-op Bank head to forge closer retail links.
newsitem.headline: New Co-op Bank head to forge closer retail links.

text.p: Britain's Co-Operative Bank Plc will forge closer links with the retail and insurance arms of its parent the Co-operative Wholesale Society (CWS), its incoming managing director said on Wednesday.
Mervyn Pedelty, who was earlier named as the successor to the Co-Op Bank's Terry Thomas, told Reuters he would "maximise the links between the retail side of the CWS and the bank'.
He said Thomas, who retires in October, had built up a great business which he had admired from the outside for many years.

Known for its ethical and environmental stance, developed under Thomas, the smallest of Britain's clearing banks has only three percent of the market but has successfully targeted higher earning customers with telephone banking and other innovations.
Pedelty, 48, said he would not alter the bank's ethical approach, which was now being adopted by others, but would work to continue its success.
But it was too early to comment on specific plans for the bank, which in April reported a 24 percent rise in annual pretax profits to January of 45.5 million pounds ($76.8 million), he said.
He takes up his post in September and will also become a member of the CWS executive with responsibility for financial services.
This appointment was, he said, recognition by the Co-Op movement of the importance of the bank and its standing within the mutual organisation as a whole.
And it showed the CWS regarded financial services as a very important part of the organisation's future.
CWS was the subject of a highly controversial 1.2 billion pound takeover attempt in April.

It succeeded in fighting off the bid but the affair brought the supermarkets-to-funeral parlours group under intense scrutiny. The Co-op Bank and CIS insurance division were both highlighted as profitable areas of business which could be spun off.
The episode also prompted calls for reform of the organisation, which was founded by a group of artisans known as the "Rochdale Pioneers" in 1844.
Pedelty said he was delighted when the bid for the CWS was "seen off" and admitted it made the task of extracting performance out of the organisation much more pertinent.

He said recent link-ups between banks and supermarkets had already been developed by the Co-op Bank and CWS retail outlets but there were opportunities to forge closer links, which would provide additional services to customers of both.
Pedelty is currently a partner of international corporate strategy consultancy firm the LEK Partnership where he specialises in financial services. Earlier he worked for the TSB Group.

"Financial services now play an expanding role in the CWS portfolio and (his) background and experience ideally equip him to develop this very important area for CWS," the bank's chairman and deputy chief executive of the CWS Alan Prescott said. ($ = 0.592 British Pounds)
